title: Mitosis and asexual reproduction
summary: How does a cell split in two, and how do living things multiply from a single parent?
cards.0.h: The cell cycle: interphase and M
cards.0.p: The time from a cell's formation to its division is called the cell cycle. The longest stage is interphase. The cell grows in G1, copies its DNA in S and prepares to divide in G2. Then come mitosis and cytokinesis, the division of the cytoplasm.
cards.0.key: DNA is copied in the S phase of interphase, not during mitosis.
cards.0.etk.soru: Put the stages of the cell cycle in order, starting with G<sub>1</sub>.
cards.1.p: The loose DNA in interphase is called chromatin. During division, chromatin shortens and thickens and is then called a chromosome. A copied chromosome is made of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere. In humans, 2n = 46.
cards.1.svg#9: number of chromosomes = number of centromeres
cards.1.key: The number of chromosomes equals the number of centromeres. A copied chromosome is still 1 chromosome, but it carries 2 chromatids. In a diploid (2n) cell, one of each pair comes from the mother and the other from the father.
cards.2.p: Prophase is the first stage of mitosis. The chromosomes become visible, and the nuclear envelope and nucleolus disappear. In an animal cell, the centrosomes move to the poles and spindle fibers form between them.
cards.2.key: Plant cells have no centrosomes, but spindle fibers still form.
cards.3.h: Metaphase: a single line at the equator
cards.3.p: In metaphase, spindle fibers attach to the centromeres, and the chromosomes line up in a single row at the equator. As you just found, the chromosomes are at their shortest and most distinct in this stage. That is why a karyotype is made in this stage.
cards.3.key: A karyotype is a picture of the chromosomes arranged in pairs by size and shape.
cards.4.p: In anaphase, the centromeres split and the sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles. Each chromatid now counts as a separate chromosome. That is why the number of chromosomes doubles for a short time.
cards.4.svg#1: each chromatid is now a chromosome
cards.4.key: In a cell with 2n = 4, the number of chromosomes becomes 8 in anaphase. The amount of DNA does not change.
cards.4.once.soru: What is pulled to opposite poles in anaphase?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: Once the centromere splits, each chromatid is pulled to its own pole.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: The nuclear envelope already disappeared in prophase.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: The centrosomes are already at the poles. What gets pulled to the poles are the chromatids.
cards.5.p: In telophase, the chromosomes loosen and the nuclear envelope forms again. Then the cytoplasm divides. This is called cytokinesis. An animal cell divides by pinching in at the middle. A plant cell builds a cell plate in the middle.
cards.5.svg#3: membrane folds in at the middle
cards.5.key: In a plant, the cell wall does not allow pinching in. That is why the plate is built from Golgi vesicles. Mitosis divides the nucleus, and cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.
cards.6.h: DNA and chromosomes stage by stage
cards.6.p: In a cell with 2n = 4, the amount of DNA rises from 2 units to 4 units in the S phase. After cytokinesis, each daughter cell gets 2 units. The number of chromosomes is 8 only in anaphase and telophase.
cards.6.key: In telophase, each new nucleus has 4 chromosomes. Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same. One 2n cell gives two 2n cells.
cards.6.once.soru: A human cell with 2n = 46 divided by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same. A 2n cell gives 2n cells again.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: The division that halves the chromosome number is meiosis.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: 92 chromosomes are seen only for a short time, in anaphase.
cards.7.h: Why mitosis matters and how it is controlled
cards.7.p: Mitosis allows growth, repair and renewal. In single-celled eukaryotes, it is also a way to reproduce. The cycle has checkpoints at G1, G2 and metaphase. If this control breaks down, cancer can develop.
cards.7.key: As a cell grows, its surface-to-volume ratio drops and division begins. Mature nerve cells do not divide.
cards.7.once.soru: Which kind of division closes a cut on your hand?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: The skin cells at the edge of the wound divide by mitosis and fill the gap.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: Cells cannot fill the gap just by growing. New cells are needed.
cards.8.p: In asexual reproduction, a single parent is enough and there is no fertilization. The offspring are genetically identical to the parent. Amoebas and euglenas divide by mitosis. A bacterium's binary fission is not mitosis, because a bacterium has no nucleus.
cards.8.svg#2: no nucleus or spindle, circular DNA
cards.8.key: Mitosis happens only in eukaryotes. In a bacterium, the circular DNA is copied and separated, and no spindle fibers form.
cards.9.p: In budding, an outgrowth forms on the parent, and it grows into a new individual. Yeast and hydras reproduce this way. In spore formation, a mold makes many spores by mitosis, and each spore can form a new individual.
cards.9.key: The offspring formed by budding is smaller than the parent. In fission, the two offspring are about the same size.
cards.9.once.soru: An outgrowth forms on a yeast cell, grows and breaks off. What kind of reproduction is this?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: A small bud grows on the parent. The offspring is smaller than the parent.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: In fission, the parent splits in two and the two offspring are about equal.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: A spore is a single cell, and many of them form inside sacs.
cards.10.p: Regrowing a lost part is called regeneration. If the broken-off piece becomes a whole individual, it counts as reproduction. Planarians reproduce this way. In parthenogenesis, an unfertilized egg develops. Male honeybees (n) form this way.
cards.10.key: In a starfish, an arm carrying part of the central disk becomes a new individual. The egg forms by meiosis, so an offspring made by parthenogenesis is not identical to its mother.
cards.10.once.soru: A lizard regrows its lost tail. Is this reproduction?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: No new individual forms. Only the lost part is regrown.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Reproduction requires a new individual. The tail does not become an individual.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.yazi: Yes, if the tail is long
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The length of the tail does not matter, because no new individual forms.
cards.11.p: Plants can make new individuals from their roots, stems or leaves. Willows are grown from cuttings, grapevines by layering and fruit trees by grafting. Potatoes spread by tubers, onions by bulbs and strawberries by runners.
cards.11.svg#18: all rely on mitosis: offspring identical to the parent
cards.11.key: In a cutting, a piece of branch takes root in the soil. In layering, a branch is buried in the soil and cut off once it roots. In grafting, the fruit has the traits of the scion, while the rootstock provides the roots and trunk.
cards.12.p: In tissue culture, a few plant cells grow into a whole plant in a sterile medium. In cloning, the nucleus of a body cell is moved into an egg whose nucleus has been removed. Dolly the sheep was born this way in 1996.
cards.12.key: Asexual reproduction is fast, and a single parent is enough. However, it does not create genetic variety.
cards.12.once.soru: Dolly's nuclear DNA is the same as which sheep's?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: The nucleus moved into the egg carries all of Dolly's nuclear DNA.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: The egg's nucleus had been removed.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: The surrogate mother only grows the embryo.
cards.13.p:
• The cell cycle is made of interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis and cytokinesis. DNA is copied in the S phase.
• Chromosomes appear in prophase, line up at the equator in metaphase, chromatids separate in anaphase and nuclei form in telophase.
• Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same.
• In asexual reproduction, the offspring are usually identical to the parent.
cards.13.svg#3: asexual reproduction: one parent, usually identical offspring
quiz.0.q: Put the events in an animal cell's cycle in order.
quiz.0.ogeler.1: Chromosomes appear and the nuclear envelope disappears
quiz.0.ogeler.2: Chromosomes line up in a single row at the equator
quiz.0.ogeler.3: Sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles
quiz.0.ogeler.4: The nuclear envelope forms again at the poles
quiz.0.ogeler.5: The cytoplasm pinches in and divides
quiz.0.e: DNA is copied in the S phase of interphase. Then chromosomes appear in prophase, line up at the equator in metaphase and their chromatids separate in anaphase. Nuclei form in telophase, and cytokinesis comes last.
quiz.1.q: A human cell with 2n = 46 chromosomes is going through mitosis. How many chromatids does this cell have in metaphase?
quiz.1.e: In the S phase, every chromosome is copied and carries two sister chromatids. That is why there are 46 × 2 = 92 chromatids.
quiz.2.q: Match each example with its type of asexual reproduction.
quiz.2.ciftler.3.0: A piece of planarian becoming an individual
quiz.2.e: An amoeba divides by mitosis, yeast buds and bread mold makes spores in a sporangium. A cut piece of planarian becomes a whole individual by regeneration. A male honeybee develops from an unfertilized egg. This is called parthenogenesis.
quiz.3.q: In a cell going through mitosis, which of these shows that it is a plant cell?
quiz.3.o.1: Chromosomes lining up at the equator
quiz.3.o.3: The cytoplasm dividing with a cell plate
quiz.3.e: Spindle fibers forming, chromosomes lining up at the equator and chromatids separating happen in both kinds of cell. A cell plate, however, forms only in plant cells.
quiz.3.y.0: Spindle fibers also form in animal cells. What is unique to plants is division with a cell plate.
quiz.3.y.1: Chromosomes line up at the equator in every mitosis. What is unique to plants is the cell plate.
quiz.3.y.2: Sister chromatids separate in the anaphase of every mitosis. What marks a plant is the cytoplasm dividing with a cell plate.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Copy the DNA, play through mitosis and divide the cell.
A:adimlar.0.metin: A cell spends most of its time in interphase, between two divisions. Move through the cycle and stop at the stage where the amount of DNA increases.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: The amount of DNA rises from 2 units to 4 units in the S phase. No new DNA is made during mitosis.
A:adimlar.1.metin: Use the switch to copy the DNA, and look at the numbers.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: How many chromosomes does this cell have once copied?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: 8 is the number of chromatids. To count chromosomes, count the centromeres.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: 4 centromeres means 4 chromosomes. The number of chromatids is 8.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The cell has two pairs, which means 4 chromosomes: 2n = 4.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Mitosis goes through four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. In this cell 2n = 4, and the DNA has already been copied. Make a guess before you play mitosis.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: In which stage does the number of chromosomes double (to 8) for a short time?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In prophase, chromosomes only shorten, thicken and become visible. There are 4 of them.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: In metaphase, chromosomes line up at the equator, but the sister chromatids are still joined. So there are 4 chromosomes.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Once the centromeres split, each chromatid counts as a separate chromosome, and the number rises from 4 to 8. The amount of DNA does not change.
A:adimlar.3.metin: To make a karyotype, you need the stage where the chromosomes are shortest, most distinct and lined up in a single row. Change the stage and find it.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: This stage is metaphase, and the chromosomes are lined up in a single row at the equator. The 46 human chromosomes are counted in this stage too.
A:adimlar.4.metin: First play the animal cell. Then switch to the plant cell and play it too.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: In a plant, Golgi vesicles join in the middle of the cell. The cell plate grows from the inside out to the edges and separates the two cells.
A:adimlar.5.metin: How does the number of bacteria grow? Make a guess before you play.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: A bacterium splits in two every 20 minutes. How many bacteria will there be after 2 hours?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The number does not go up by 1 with each division. It doubles.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: There are 6 divisions in 2 hours. But the number of bacteria is not equal to the number of divisions.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: There are 6 divisions in 120 minutes, and the number doubles with each one. The result is 2⁶ = 64 bacteria.
A:adimlar.6.metin: In grafting, a piece of branch from one plant (the scion) is joined to the roots and trunk of another plant (the rootstock).
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: A scion of a sweet apple variety was grafted onto a sour wild apple rootstock. What fruit will the grafted branch bear?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The rootstock provides the roots and trunk. The branch and fruit develop from the scion.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: There is no fertilization in grafting, and the inherited traits do not mix. The branch grows from the scion's own cells by mitosis.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The branch and fruit develop from the scion's cells by mitosis and are genetically the same as the scion. Gardeners copy a variety they like by grafting, without waiting for seeds.
A:kapanis.0: The cell cycle is made of interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis and cytokinesis. DNA is copied in the S phase.
A:kapanis.1: The number of chromosomes equals the number of centromeres. A copied chromosome carries two sister chromatids.
A:kapanis.2: The stages of mitosis are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. The chromosome number is doubled only in anaphase and telophase. Mitosis ends with two 2n cells.
A:kapanis.3: Cytokinesis happens by pinching in in animal cells and with a cell plate in plant cells.
A:kapanis.4: In asexual reproduction, the offspring are genetically identical to the parent. A bacterium's binary fission is not mitosis. In grafting, the fruit has the traits of the scion.
